images.title: Nine children with hats and flags
images.purpose: Give the student a small practice picture of 9 children, some with a hat, some with a flag, some with both and some with neither, to count and compare before the statements are judged.
images.composition: Nine simple children in one row: two with a hat and a flag, two with only a hat, three with only a flag and two with neither, with the caption Nine children.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Exactly 9 children stand in one row on a line at y 640, their head centres at x 128, 278, 428, 578, 728, 878, 1028, 1178 and 1328 (150 px apart), all the same size and facing the front. Every child is flat: a white round head (radius 38, centre y 340, thin dark #2B2B2B outline 3 px, two dot eyes and a small smile), a rounded-rectangle body 70 px wide filled construction grey #6B7280 (y 385 to 535), two dark #2B2B2B legs (20 px wide, y 535 to 640) and two thin arms. A HAT is an amber #E69F00 triangle (64 px wide at its base on the top of the head at y 302, apex at y 240) with a thin dark outline. A FLAG is held in the child's right hand (the viewer's right): a thin dark pole (4 px) rising 130 px from the hand (x = child centre + 55, y 455 up to y 325) with a teal #0072B2 rectangular flag 50 by 34 px at the top of the pole, pointing right (x centre + 55 to centre + 105, y 325 to 359); the other arm hangs down. A child with no flag has both arms hanging down. From left to right: child 1 has a hat and a flag, child 2 has a hat and a flag, child 3 has only a hat, child 4 has only a hat, child 5 has only a flag, child 6 has only a flag, child 7 has only a flag, child 8 has neither, child 9 has neither. So the frame has 4 hats, 5 flags and 9 children (2 with a hat and a flag, 2 with only a hat, 3 with only a flag, 2 with neither). The small caption Nine children is centred at (728, 730) in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). No other text and no counts. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 9 children, 4 hats or 5 flags, or children in an order other than hat and flag twice, hat twice, flag three times, neither twice
any count, total or statement written in the frame other than the caption
a child with a half hat, a hidden flag or a flag held on the wrong side
images.takeaway: Counting the children the statement talks about, and comparing the counts, shows whether a statement about the picture is true or false.
images.description: Nine children in a row: the first two have a hat and a flag, the next two a hat only, the next three a flag only and the last two have neither.
images.context: Concept image for Counting and Comparing in a Picture. It follows the idea of the book's picture of school children with hats, flags and other things to count, and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 9 children, 4 with hats, 5 with flags and 2 with both.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student count the hats, the flags and the children with both before judging a statement: hats 2 + 2 = 4, flags 2 + 3 = 5. The slip to watch: judging the statement at a quick look instead of counting.

image_decisions.why: Nine children in a row, some with a hat, some with a flag, some with both and some with neither, give a practice picture to count before judging statements.
